findings: NON-BLOCKER (carried from gen2, unchanged): explicit opts.timeoutMs is honored verbatim with no floor/validation (0 or negative aborts near-instantly), asymmetric with the validated EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_MS env path. Still verified unreachable in production this generation — no new callsite introduced. No code touched by this delta, so the finding stands as-is.

NON-BLOCKER (carried from gen1, re-verified): Postgres Float[] round-trip changes the last significant digit (~1e-16 relative). This generation's own gen3 wipe-attack test hit the exact same artifact when comparing a freshly-written vector against a fresh DB read — fixed by comparing against the DB's own previously-round-tripped bytes where an exact match is expected (untouched column) and by tolerance (<1e-12) where a genuinely new write is expected. No product-level implication.

NON-BLOCKER (carried from gen1, re-verified): hybridScore's dim-mismatch early return precedes its outcome-0 guard, but every production recall path routes through recallHybrid's suppressedKeys, which still zeroes negative-outcome rows end-to-end.
RESOLVED in gen2, re-verified in gen3: recordHumanDecision embedding store/skip now has both mocked-unit and real-DB integration coverage.

OBSERVATION (new, non-blocker): the fix's guard (`input.embedding && input.embedding.length > 0`) treats ANY empty array as 'no embedding', including a deliberate future intent to clear a vector. There is currently no product code path that ever wants to explicitly clear a stored embedding (deletion goes through row deletion, not embedding: []), so this is not reachable as a regression today; flagged only for awareness if a future feature needs an explicit-clear semantic (it would need a distinct sentinel, e.g. `null`, not `[]`).
